# Results

*Generated by `python -m arxiv_search.evaluate.experiments`. Don't edit by hand.*

Each row is one search system, best first. Scores are against each query's source paper:
**R@k** = share of queries whose source paper is in the top k; **MRR@10** = average of
1 ÷ its rank (0 if below 10), with a 95% interval. **Δ vs baseline** is the paired
difference from `bm25-baseline` on the same queries: if its interval excludes 0, the
difference is real. The columns *keyword* to *broad* are MRR@10 within that group (dev:
25 per type, 74 specific, 26 broad). Broad queries have many right answers, so their
scores are a lower bound until the LLM judge grades other papers (nDCG@10 comes then).

**Careful:** picking the best of many rows on 100 dev queries flatters the winner a
little (winner's curse). The honest score is the finalist's run on test.

## Relevance judge calibration (separate from retrieval scores)

### Judge pilot (rubric b8b0c14a)

12 dev queries, 266 query-paper pairs. Human grades so far: 100.

Preliminary calibration on one person's pilot labels, not held-out validation. Models with different coverage must be compared on the same pair subset. OpenAI's human-only run intentionally grades 100 pairs, not all 266 pooled pairs.

| Judge | Pairs graded | Calls | Mean s/call | Source papers graded 2 | Grade 0/1/2 shares |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemma-31b | 266 / 266 | 18 | 106 | 12 / 12 | 47% / 42% / 11% |
| qwen2.5-7b | 263 / 266 | 12 | 625 | 5 / 9 | 44% / 51% / 5% |
| openai-nano | 100 / 266 | 13 | 3 | 11 / 12 | 29% / 46% / 25% |
| openai-mini | 100 / 266 | 13 | 3 | 11 / 12 | 42% / 35% / 23% |
| openai-4.1-mini | 100 / 266 | 13 | 3 | 12 / 12 | 25% / 40% / 35% |
| openai-4o-mini | 100 / 266 | 13 | 3 | 10 / 12 | 29% / 49% / 22% |

**Exact** = same grade. **κ** = Cohen's kappa (1 perfect, 0 chance; quadratic: 0-vs-2 costs most). **Relevant** = agree on 0 vs 1-or-2. **Opposite** = one said 0, the other 2.

| Comparison | Pairs | Exact | κ (quadratic) | Relevant agree | κ (relevant) | Opposite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**Metric definitions:** linear-gain nDCG@10; P@10 counts grades 1 and 2 as relevant; unjudged papers count as zero. All systems use the same pooled labels plus human overrides for ideal DCG. Original graded.SYSTEMS top-10s remain in the pool. Unjudged gains are zero; nDCG with no positive labels is undefined. Source-paper metrics are separate. Candidate outputs contain up to 100 papers; a depth-20 union can be shorter.

Exploratory dev results, not held-out confirmation; no reranker. Judge calibration used one person's pilot labels, not independent validation. Paired 95% intervals are query-bootstrap intervals conditional on these labels, without multiple-comparison correction. Deltas are candidate minus fixed baseline.

## Frozen baseline failure analysis

# Frozen baseline failure analysis

Judge `openai-mini`, rubric `b8b0c14a`. 100 dev queries; no API calls or label changes.
Cases are diagnostic leads, not proven causes. Read full abstracts and label provenance in cases.json. A judge reason is not ground truth.
